newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares fall on U.S. figures, weaker dollar.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares fall on U.S. figures, weaker dollar.

text.p: Swedish shares fell on Friday, following stronger-than-expected U.S. December jobs data, a weaker dollar and profit taking.
The general index dropped 1.48 percent to 2,399.55 in turnover of 5.77 billion crowns.
The forestry sector fell 1.71 percent on the softer dollar.
Telecoms group Ericsson shed two crowns, landing at 224 on profit taking after surging for two consecutive days, up four crowns on Thursday and 14 crowns on Wednesday.
U.S. rival Motorola's fourth quarter earnings report released on Thursday should not affect Ericsson, analysts said.
"Although prices fell today, it is really nothing compared to how much it has risen in recent days," a trader said.
On Monday, developments will depend what will happen in New York on Friday, dealers said.
Automotive group Volvo belonged to shares hit by profit taking, down 4.5 crowns to 156.
The bank and insurance sector also fell, down 1.6 percent, partly on higher bond yields and partly on profit taking.
But banking group Swedbank bucked negative trends and rose 1.5 crowns to 114. Dealers could not explain why.
